Our own descriptions; shots after 125 s are sparse samples. Xplained with Mushrooms, 622K views, 2.3K subs.

lines.gist: You send a question and words appear a second later
Most think it looked it up; it did not, there is no library
So where do the words come from? One picture will explain it
Mushroom root webs: threads thicken where more travels
Training thickens the thread between words seen together
What it was fed; the encyclopedia was the smallest share; myths grow thick too
Books gone, threads are numbers, word pieces, your question as a spore, no plan
Randomness, context window, made-up answers, weak maths
The 2017 paper, scale, manners training, agreeing, hidden instructions, the debate
It is weakest exactly where the roots are thin, yet sounds just as sure
Back to pressing send: nothing looked up, one piece at a time

ending.lastFrame: soil box of roots with a glowing spore

whyItWorks: One everyday metaphor (mushroom roots) carries every concept; each new idea is a new thing done to the roots.
The hook kills the viewer's wrong guess (it looks things up) in 12 s, then asks the real question.
Short chapters about every 30-40 s, each named as a question or claim, so there is always a next small payoff.
No music, no captions: a calm voice over warm storybook pictures, with tiny animated loops on literal moments.
